page: Microsoft Azure M128-32ms is an ultra-high-memory instance belonging to Azure's memory-optimized MS family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system is driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration exposes 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with two threads per core, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache. It features an exceptionally high memory footprint of 3,892.0 GB, allocating roughly 121.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is addressed through 4,398 GB of local SSD capacity, while GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a performance profile heavily focused on RAM throughput rather than raw compute velocity. The instance demonstrates strong memory write capabilities on large uncached 256 MB blocks at 135.69 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile of evaluated machines. Its multi-threaded processing registers within average brackets, reflected by a stress-ng multi-core score of 21,882.64, a PassMark CPU score of 21,694.3, and Redis throughput of 21.11 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 900.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1,038.39. Text compression and decompression tasks exhibit comparable single-threaded limitations.

From an infrastructure perspective, the M128-32ms offers high resource concentration when memory density is the primary architectural requirement. Instead of scaling horizontally across standard multi-core nodes, this instance consolidates massive dataset footprints into a single operational domain. The primary trade-off involves subdued per-thread computational throughput relative to newer processor generations. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for enterprise in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive operational caches, and in-memory analytics engines that require vast memory pools paired with local SSD scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure M128-32ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for extreme memory-to-core requirements. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor running at 2.7 GHz, the instance delivers 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyperthreading on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides an extensive 3,892 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 121.62 GB per vCPU, alongside 4,398 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark results show strong memory write bandwidth of 135.69 GB/sec on large uncached transfers, paired with average multi-threaded performance, as indicated by a PassMark CPU score of 21,694.3 and 21.11 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects lower generational performance metrics, represented by a Geekbench single-core score of 900.0. The architecture is specialized for workloads where memory density outweighs per-thread compute velocity, making it suitable for massive in-memory databases, large cache layers, and heavy enterprise transaction processing engines.
